findings.title: Config save still issues GET to a POST-only, body-driven backend route
findings.problem: The diff adds the optional `body` parameter to RestService.post() explicitly to support the config-set POST migration (recent commits fffa81a/fe0e07d migrated the backend GET->POST), but the only caller that needs it was not updated. ConfigService.set() still calls `this._restService.sendRequest(url)` (an HTTP GET) against `/server/config/set/${section}/${option}/${value}`. The backend registers that path via `web_app.add_post_handler("/server/config/set", ...)` — POST-only, no path params, reading `section`/`key`/`value` from `bottle.request.json`. So every config save from the UI hits a route that no longer exists for GET: it 404s (or is swallowed by the SPA catch-all, as the backend test at test_config.py:226 notes), the WebReaction comes back unsuccessful, and the local `_config` BehaviorSubject is never updated. Note the body field name is `key`, not `option`, and the value must NOT be double-URI-encoded as the current caller does.
findings.fix_hint: call this._restService.post("/server/config/set", {section, key: option, value: valueStr}) — drop CONFIG_SET_URL and the double encodeURIComponent, since the value now travels in the JSON body
findings.why_it_matters: Every settings change in the UI silently fails to persist; the user sees an error (or nothing) and the in-memory config diverges from the server.

findings.title: Frontend config.set() still sends GET to removed path-param route — config saving is broken end-to-end
findings.problem: The backend was migrated in commit 386f68c: src/python/web/handler/config.py now registers `/server/config/set` via `web_app.add_post_handler` (POST only, no path params) and reads `section`/`key`/`value` from `bottle.request.json`. The frontend was NOT migrated in lockstep. config.service.ts:22 still builds `CONFIG_SET_URL = /server/config/set/${section}/${option}/${value}` and line 66 still calls `this._restService.sendRequest(url)` — an HTTP GET against a URL shape that no longer has a registered route. Every settings save in the UI will 404 (the integration test at src/python/tests/integration/test_web/test_handler/test_config.py:226 documents that a GET to /server/config/set is intercepted by the SPA catch-all). This diff adds the `body` parameter to RestService.post — the enabling half of the migration — but no caller was updated to use it, so the capability is added and left unwired. Whether this is intentional wave sequencing or a dropped hand-off, the tree as it stands has a broken settings page: backend POST-only, frontend GET-only, zero overlap.

const url = this.CONFIG_SET_URL(section, option, valueEncoded);
const obs = this._restService.sendRequest(url);
findings.fix_hint: Migrate config.service.ts to `this._restService.post("/server/config/set", {section, key: option, value})` and drop the double encodeURIComponent (the body is JSON, not a path segment); update config.service.spec.ts expectations to POST.
findings.why_it_matters: Backend and frontend now disagree on both HTTP verb and payload location for the config-set endpoint. If shipped in this state, no user can change any setting — Sonarr/Radarr URLs, API keys, paths, debug flags — from the web UI. This is a complete outage of the settings surface, not a degradation.

findings.title: `body ?? null` erases the Content-Type header Angular would otherwise infer, so bottle.request.json returns None
findings.problem: HttpClient infers `Content-Type: application/json` from the body's runtime type. An object body gets the JSON content type; `null` does not (no body, no inferred type). That coalescing is correct for the three existing no-body callers, but the new backend handler depends on the header being present: config.py's comment states explicitly that with a wrong or absent content-type, `bottle.request.json` "returns None silently" — which the handler then maps to a 400 "Invalid request body". So the object path must actually carry the header. Angular's inference does handle a plain object literal, but this is fragile in two concrete ways: (a) a caller passing an already-serialized string would be typed out by `body?: object` yet a `new String()` or a class instance with a custom `toJSON` can serialize unexpectedly; (b) if any future interceptor clones the request with `setHeaders` before the body serializer runs, the inferred type can be lost. Marked pending: I did not execute a request to observe the wire headers — the mechanism is read from Angular's serializer contract and config.py's own comment, not measured.
findings.fix_hint: Set the header explicitly on the object path rather than relying on inference: when body is provided, pass `{responseType: "text", headers: {"Content-Type": "application/json"}}`.
findings.why_it_matters: A silently-absent Content-Type does not fail loudly — bottle returns None, the handler returns a generic 400 "Invalid request body", and the UI shows a save failure with no diagnostic. That failure mode is indistinguishable from a validation rejection, which makes it expensive to debug in the field.

findings.title: MockRestService has no `post` method at all — any spec exercising the new body path against the mock fails at runtime
findings.problem: MockRestService exposes only `sendRequest`; it has no `post` stub, let alone a two-arg one. It is imported by the autoqueue, model-file, server-command, config, and version-check specs. Today that is latent — those specs spy on the injected instance rather than call through — but the moment config.service.ts is migrated to `post(url, body)` (finding impact-001), the config spec's mock has no method to spy on and `spyOn(mockRestService, "post")` throws "post() method does not exist". The mock is the shared seam for five spec files, so it must be widened as part of the same change, not after.
findings.fix_hint: Add `public post(_url: string, _body?: object): Observable<WebReaction> { return null!; }` (and a `delete` stub) so the mock's surface matches RestService.
findings.why_it_matters: The mock silently drifting from the real service turns a mechanical signature change into five confusing spec failures in unrelated suites, which is the kind of breakage that gets 'fixed' by weakening assertions rather than by widening the mock.

findings.title: rest.service.spec.ts covers only sendRequest — the changed post() method has zero direct test coverage
findings.problem: The spec file for the changed file has four tests, all against `sendRequest` (GET). There is no test asserting that `post(url)` still sends a null body, that `post(url, {a: 1})` sends that object, or — most importantly given the backend's content-type sensitivity — that the outgoing request carries `Content-Type: application/json` when a body is present. The one behavioral guarantee this diff's JSDoc explicitly claims ("when omitted, sends null (preserving prior no-body callers)") is untested, so a future refactor to `body || null` or `body ?? undefined` would regress the three restart/model-file callers with nothing to catch it.

findings.fix_hint: Add two HttpTestingController cases: `post(url)` → expect `req.request.body` toBeNull, and `post(url, {section:"a"})` → expect body toEqual the object and `req.request.detectContentTypeHeader()` / headers.get("Content-Type") to be application/json.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the exact seam the config-set migration depends on. Shipping the enabling parameter with no test pins the contract only by convention, and the null-preservation promise is the thing three existing production callers silently rely on.
